about: READ-ONLY: renders what `reclaim-gcp-root` WOULD remove on boss-gcp, and removes nothing (infra/gcp/reclaim-gcp-root.sh --dry-run; backlog d3c7eada car 2). It runs every bound the write runs — the two fixed globs /opt/boss-binbak-* and /opt/boss-dev-bak, real directories only, nothing changed (ctime) in 30 days, nothing live: no live tree, mount, symlink, running process, loaded unit or unit file on disk resolving into one — and the capture bound — the retired second stack's database capture, the one exception under /var/backups (David, 2026-09-28, backlog f44ca628): only /var/backups/boss/second-stack/second-stack-*.sql, each named ^second-stack-[0-9]{8}T[0-9]{6}Z\.sql$, a regular file (no symlink) directly in a directory with no link on the way, no mount point, held open by no process, with no age bound — and the dump bound — the dumps the retired boss-gcp off-site leg deposited, the second exception under /var/backups (David, 2026-10-01, backlog 4bf7bdd1: the GCS bucket is the off-site copy): only /var/backups/boss-cluster-pg/boss-*.sql.gz, each named ^boss-[A-Za-z0-9._:+-]+\.sql\.gz$, a regular file with one link directly in a directory writable by no group and no other account inside a root-owned closed parent, no mount point, held open by no process, with no age bound — and then prints the plan: each candidate's path, size in MiB and top-level entries, sorted; each capture's path, size in bytes and sha256, so the passkey signs those exact bytes; each dump's path, size, inode, mtime and ctime (its identity — no dump's bytes are read), and the dump directory's owner and mode; each candidate holding a .git as KEPT, not removed (a checkout may carry unpushed commits), with its unpushed state as evidence — except /opt/boss-dev-bak, which it lists FIRST for REMOVAL, with that evidence as its proof, when every checkout in it (nested ones included) was read and every count is 0 — the counts including commits on any ref on no configured remote, linked worktrees under .git/worktrees and submodule repositories under .git/modules, with only the refs of remotes its config names counting as pushed, and only of a remote whose every URL is a network URL, each URL printed with its userinfo stripped; a remote at a local path, file:// or anything else keeps the checkout (David, 2026-09-30, backlog d3c7eada: it is disposable; adversarial review 2435f065) — local branches with commits on no remote (the first 20 named, all counted, so the plan stays under the runner cap), commits at HEAD on no branch and no remote, staged changes, tracked files whose bytes differ from the index (hashed without filters), untracked files and stashes, measured against its own remote-tracking refs (it never fetches), or why that could not be read. The checkout is read with plumbing that runs no command its config names (no filter, fsmonitor, hook or gpg), with a scrubbed git environment and GIT_NO_LAZY_FETCH, and never as root: as its owner through setpriv, and a root-owned checkout as nobody (uid 65534); a checkout whose config names a partial clone or a promisor remote is not read at all (a missing object would make git fetch through that remote), and is kept; and the fixed journal line (vacuum to 1G). No clock, free space or journal usage in the bytes (those ride stderr); its sha256 is printed on stderr as `plan-sha256:`, and that hash is what David's passkey signs (design 17835005 q1). Any refusal renders no plan. A plan that is the journal line ALONE names nothing to do (`nothing_to_do`, backlog b2f78bb9): nothing to remove, and the converge caps this host's journal at 256M (infra/gcp/journald-cap.conf), so the fixed vacuum to 1G changes nothing; the runner closes such a request through its nothing-to-do terminal, with the plan on it, and asks nobody for a passkey. A plan that keeps a checkout is still shown to a person.
